subject: XDIFF rows column in perl-suite-expected.tsv — machine-checked like FIXTURE
description:
DONE s336 (commit c4a128e). XDIFF is granted per ROW, all-or-nothing like FIXTURE.

DEVIATION from the task text (flagged in docs/opus5-review-requests-s336.md):
the rows live in a SIDECAR, docs/perl-suite-expected-rows.tsv, not as a column
in perl-suite-expected.tsv — 1720 generated rows inside the reason registry
would drown its 108 hand-written reasons. Same enforcement either way.

Shape: one line per diverging row, `rel<TAB>rowkey`. rowkey = PERL's test
DESCRIPTION (#177), with "#N" for unnamed tests, "*extra* <desc>" for a
PCL-only TAP row, "*summary*", "*no-log*". Compared as a MULTISET.
Unregistered diverging row -> file stays DIFF and names the intruder;
registered row that stops diverging -> STALE. `--bless-rows` regenerates,
touching only files the run measured. Both directions verified by deliberately
breaking the baseline (op/crypt.t).

Stability measured over 4 full runs of the 108 files: A/B agree on 107.
mro/package_aliases_utf8.t is nondeterministic two ways (PCL-only rows
54/34/34, one run TIMEOUT not DIFF) and holds the one *rows-unstable* opt-out
(hand-placed only; --bless-rows never invents or overwrites it). Verification
run D: 108 files / 108 XDIFF / 0 UNEXPLAINED.

Also fixed: unnamed rowkeys are perl's "[at <file> line N]" marker and baked
the build-machine path into the artifact (#217 family) — $tdir stripped to t/.
